proposals.title: Daily Task for AI Usage Credits
proposals.oneLiner: Play a 15-second mini-game with Luzia to earn daily AI usage credits.

newMechanic.name: Daily Tasks
newMechanic.description: A new interactive banner on the Chats Home screen offering daily mini-game challenges for AI usage credits.
newMechanic.whyNeeded: Increases daily engagement and retention by gamifying the AI experience.

proposals.trigger: User taps the Daily Task banner on the Chats Home (s01) tab.
proposals.eligibility: Non-subscribers, once per day per user.

offer.title: Daily Task: Earn Credits
offer.body: Play a quick 15-second mini-game with Luzia to earn 5 extra AI usage credits.

proposals.cannibalizationGuard: Only offered to non-subscribers. The credits are additive to their quota and do not provide the advanced capabilities of the Luzia+ subscription. The banner is non-interruptive.
risks: High frequency of tasks could feel repetitive if not rotated.
Potential for users to rely on credits instead of subscribing.

newElements.change: Add a Daily Task banner element to provide a clear entry point for rewarded mini-games.

newMechanic.name: Daily Tasks
newMechanic.description: A new interactive banner on the Chats Home (s01) screen offering daily mini-game challenges for AI usage credits.
newMechanic.whyNeeded: Increases daily engagement and retention for non-subscribers by gamifying AI usage while protecting margins.

proposals.trigger: User taps the Daily Task banner on the Chats Home (s01) tab, outside of their first session.
proposals.eligibility: Returning non-subscribers (session 2+), once per day per user.

offer.title: Daily Task: Earn Credits
offer.body: Play a quick 15-second mini-game with Luzia to earn 2 extra AI usage credits.

proposals.cannibalizationGuard: Only offered to non-subscribers and returning users (session 2+). Credits are additive to the usage quota and do not unlock the advanced capabilities or reasoning modes of the Luzia+ subscription. The reward is sized to maintain a healthy margin per view.
risks: If not rotated, mini-game tasks may become repetitive.
Potential for users to rely on ad-earned credits instead of subscribing if limits are miscalculated.

proposals.title: Unlock Image Generation Credit

newMechanic.name: Rewarded Image Credits
newMechanic.description: Users can watch or play a mini-game to earn an image generation credit when they hit their AI usage quota.
newMechanic.whyNeeded: Allows free users to continue generating images without impacting paid conversion by limiting the reward to a single credit per view.

proposals.trigger: When user attempts to generate an image in the Image Creation Hub and their AI Usage Quota (r3) is depleted.
proposals.eligibility: Non-paying users who have exhausted their free AI Usage Quota (r3).

offer.title: Earn an image credit
offer.body: Play a 15-second game with Luzia to get 1 free AI image generation credit.

proposals.cannibalizationGuard: Limited to 3 credits per day and only available when r3 is depleted; ensures non-payers maintain usage without unlimited free generation.

kpis.holdout: 10% of non-paying user base held out for 4 weeks.

risks: Ad saturation if limits are too frequent
Brand safety concerns in AI-generated images
Potential for lower paid conversion if reward is too generous

proposals.title: Paywall-decline: Deep Reasoning Sample
proposals.oneLiner: Offer a 1-hour trial of Deep Reasoning mode after declining the account signup wall.

newMechanic.name: Rewarded Deep Reasoning Trial
newMechanic.description: A time-boxed (1 hour) trial of Deep Reasoning mode triggered by an ad after the user declines the account signup wall on s07.
newMechanic.whyNeeded: Deep Reasoning is a core premium differentiator; letting users experience it creates high conversion intent.

proposals.trigger: After the user taps 'Close' to decline the account signup wall that appeared when they tried to toggle 'Deep reasoning' (m9) or 'Start a task' (m10).
proposals.eligibility: Non-paying guests who are not currently on a subscription and have triggered the Luzia+ paywall.

offer.title: Try Deep Reasoning for free
offer.body: Play a quick 15-second game to unlock 1 hour of our premium Deep Reasoning mode.

proposals.cannibalizationGuard: This offer is only presented to users who have already explicitly declined the paywall. It provides a limited, time-boxed trial rather than permanent access, protecting the subscription value and highlighting the benefit of Luzia+.

kpis.holdout: 5% user holdout for 4 weeks to measure revenue impact.

risks: Ad availability (no-fill) may frustrate users who have just declined the paywall; mitigation is an immediate fallback to the original state.
High COGS for the premium model; mitigation is the 1-hour time box.

evidence.quote: To enjoy Luzia+ you need to create an account first.

proposals.title: Sponsored Advanced Services 30m Trial
proposals.oneLiner: Offer a 30-minute trial of Luzia+ Advanced services after declining the account wall.

newMechanic.name: Rewarded Trial Access
newMechanic.description: After a user dismisses the Create Account wall, surface an opt-in rewarded ad to unlock 30 minutes of Luzia+ Advanced services (bookings/alerts).
newMechanic.whyNeeded: Allows high-intent, cash-poor users to experience premium value, increasing conversion probability while monetizing users who would otherwise churn at the paywall.

proposals.trigger: User taps 'Maybe later' on the Create Account Sheet (s07) after attempting a premium-gated task.
proposals.eligibility: Non-subscribers who have not hit the daily cap for rewarded trials.

offer.title: Try Advanced Services
offer.body: Watch a 15-second game to get 30 minutes of Advanced Services (bookings & alerts) for free.

proposals.cannibalizationGuard: The trial is time-boxed (30m) and limited to 1x/day, protecting the long-term value of the subscription while creating a clear sampling effect. The offer appears only as a fallback to account creation, ensuring purchase remains the primary path.
risks: Advanced services are compute-intensive (text-premium COGS); trial usage must be throttled to prevent excess costs.
Users may perceive the ad path as sufficient and not upgrade.
